newsitem.title: UK: Sainsbury's Bank deposits top 600 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: Sainsbury's Bank deposits top 600 mln stg.

text.p: British supermarket retailer J. Sainsbury Plc's banking joint venture now has over 600 million stg in deposits, Sainsbury's Bank deputy chief executive Richard Chadwick told Reuters on Wednesday.
"We have over 600 million (stg) in deposits, we are still opening accounts at the rate of over 12,000 a week," he said.

Sainsbury's Bank is 55 percent owned by Sainsbury and 45 percent by Bank of Scotland and offers an instant access savings account, a Christmas savings account, two types of credit card and personal loans.

It launched mortgages earlier this week, offering a variable rate of 7.45 percent per year for mortgages up to 75 percent of the property value and a rate of 7.9 percent for loans between 75 percent and 95 percent.
The Sainsbury's Bank mortgage also allows customers to pay over 10 months instead of 12 and to have a six months break from repayments.
For endowment and personal equity plan (PEP) backed mortgages, Sainsbury's Bank has teamed up with Europe's largest mutual insurer Standard Life, of which it is a tied agent.
Sainsbury's Bank was launched on February 19.
